content:
customer_acme: Hey team — after we enabled the int8 quant profile on our Dedicated instance the embeddings API started returning vectors of length 1536 instead of 768. Similarity scores dropped badly. Anyone seen this?

sam_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the API request/response (sanitized) and clarify whether you changed model version + quant profile at the same time?

customer_acme: We only flipped the quant_profile flag under our model-config in the console. Request sample: `POST /v1/embeddings {
  "model": "redwood-embed-large",
  "input": ["test text"]
}` Response snippet: `{"data": [{"embedding": [..1536 numbers..]}]}` We didn't change model name.

maria_ops: Quick repro check: in python you can assert with: `len(resp['data'][0]['embedding'])` — did you try that? Also can you share the deployment config (quant_profile name) you picked?

customer_acme: Repro steps we did: 1) toggle quant_profile to `int8_aggressive`, 2) restart pool, 3) send batch of 8 texts. Console shows active model: redwood-embed-large (no variant suffix).

jordan_ml: Interesting — two hypotheses: 1) the int8 profile picks a quantized variant that has a different pooling head (vector concat) OR 2) serving fallback routed you to a different model binary that appends token-level pooled features. Can you grab the full response headers? We log `x-redwood-model-variant` and `x-quant-profile` in headers.

customer_acme: Headers: `x-redwood-model-variant: redwood-embed-large-v2-int8concat`, `x-quant-profile: int8_aggressive`, `x-request-id: rq_32b9`

sam_support: That header is a smoking gun. Looks like the int8 aggressive profile routed to a variant with concatenated outputs (v2-int8concat). Not intended to be used as a drop-in replacement for v1.

ryan_infra: Confirming from infra logs for rq_32b9: the pool didn't have the standard int8-compat variant, so smart-routing picked v2-int8concat as a capacity-compatible fallback. Routing policy flagged it as "compatible" which is technically true but incompatible for dimensionality expectations.

maria_ops: Immediate mitigation: flip quant_profile back to `fp16_standard` or explicitly pin `model_variant: redwood-embed-large-v1` in your model-config. We'll also add a server-side dim check to reject incompatible variants.

customer_acme: Pinning to v1 fixed it immediately, embedding length back to 768. Thanks. Any ETA on a more permanent guard?

jordan_ml: Action items: 1) Add a validation in the embeddings endpoint that checks response length against model metadata and returns 400 with a helpful message when a mismatch occurs. 2) Update routing rules so fallback variants must match embedding-dim metadata, not only architecture compatibility. 3) Add a note to the console UI: quant profiles may pick different model variants that change output shape — show a warning.

support-bot: created ticket INFR-4921 "embeddings: validate embedding dimension on response and disallow incompatible variant fallback" assigned to eng-runtime.

ryan_infra: Quick short-term patch deployed to canary: we now annotate `x-variant-dim` header and we reject requests where `expected_dim != x-variant-dim` (400). Canary rolled to 2 regions.

maria_ops: Follow-up for docs/devex: add a FAQ entry on quant profiles vs embedding shape and sample code to assert embedding length on the client. Recommend clients assert length and surface an error when mismatch occurs.

customer_acme: Thanks all — will keep pinned for now and test with smaller batches. FYI we saw the issue more when batching 8+ inputs; single requests routed fine because they hit a different pool.

jordan_ml: Noted — batching changed routing probability because of capacity bins. Longer term we'll make routing aware of expected shape regardless of batch size.

sam_support: Closing loop: for anyone who hits this: check `x-redwood-model-variant` and `x-variant-dim` headers, pin model_variant if you need strict stability, or use `fp16_standard` quant profile. File INFR-4921 tracks the engineering fix. :thumbsup:
